Quick internal summary after review of Claire's files:

Top priority items to resolve before our call with HelioStack:
1) DPA: their spreadsheet requests a 30-day data export guarantee and a narrower definition of "processing" that would exclude certain telemetry we collect. We should push back; propose 90 days for export support (aligned with our retention policy) and keep telemetry in the processing definition but scope it for operational use only.
2) MSA: they added a limitation of liability cap tied to annual spend; they want a carveout for indemnities related to IP claims. We can accept a mutual IP indemnity clause but need to keep our commercial cap consistent across partners.
3) Encryption/KMS: confirm support for customer KMS in Dedicated, and propose a standard SOW appendix for deployment-level key management.
4) SOW milestones: the connector mapping milestone is fine; suggest adding acceptance criteria and a 14-day acceptance period after delivery instead of immediate sign-off.

Recommended next steps:
- Laura to draft redline suggestions for MSA/DPA (I'll add inline comments).
- Jonas to pull commercial team if we need to adjust cap structures.
- Book 30-min sync with HelioStack on Thu 10/12 or Fri 11/12 PT — Claire suggested next week.

One-line: we push on DPA timelines and the LoC/IP carveouts; otherwise we can close quickly with language tweaks.

Vanessa Ortiz
Sr. Legal Ops, Redwood Inference

Thanks team — I reviewed Claire's redlines and Vanessa's summary. A few legal positions we should take (draft language attached):

- DPA: Acceptable to offer 30-day export assistance operationally but cannot contractually guarantee permanent export success beyond 90 days after termination; propose the following clause: "Provider will make commercially reasonable efforts to assist in data export for a period of 90 days following termination."

- Processing definition: keep telemetry in the processing definition but limit downstream usage: "Telemetry used solely for service operation and security, aggregated or anonymized for analytics; not used to train models without customer consent." This addresses privacy concerns.

- Liability/indemnity: For IP indemnities, propose a mutual indemnity limited to third-party IP claims, with usual carveouts for open-source components. Cap remain at the higher of (i) six months' fees or (ii) $250,000. If HelioStack insists on spend-tied cap, request a reciprocal structure.

- Encryption appendix: I'll draft an appendix that references customer-managed KMS and the responsibilities for key rotation and access logs.

I'll attach a redlined MSA with my proposed edits. If commercial accepts the cap levels above we can send consolidated language to HelioStack; otherwise we should escalate to execs for approval.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Claire / Mark —

Appreciate the thorough review and the quick turnaround from your side. Attached are our consolidated positions and suggested redline language for the MSA/DPA/SOW. High level summary:

- DPA/export: Redwood can operationally support export assistance for 90 days post-termination and will provide documented instructions and a small transition window. We cannot commit to indefinite export guarantees in the MSA; see proposed clause in the redline.
- Processing/telemetry: telemetry remains within the definition of processing but we added a clause restricting training on raw telemetry data without explicit consent.
- Liability: proposed mutual IP indemnity; cap proposal is the higher of six months' fees or $250k. If HelioStack needs a spend-tied cap, we are open to reciprocal terms but will need a commercial exception approved.
- KMS/encryption: Redwood Dedicated supports customer-managed keys; we included an appendix to the SOW with responsibilities for key custody and rotation.
- SOW: accepted connector mapping milestone and added acceptance criteria plus a 14-day acceptance window.

Next steps:
1) Please review the attached marked-up MSA/DPA (MSA_redline_JW_v2.docx, DPA_comments_JW.xlsx) and indicate any non-starters.
2) If HelioStack agrees in principle, propose a short legal-to-legal call Monday 15 Dec at 10am PT to finalize carveouts and get to DocuSign.

If there are any items that are commercial exceptions (cap change), I'll flag them internally and get back to you within 24 hours.

Thanks — talk soon.

Jonas Weber
